newsitem.title: REUNION: Sputnik replica to bleep again from space.
newsitem.headline: Sputnik replica to bleep again from space.

text.p: A replica of the Sputnik satellite, built by Russian and French students, will go into orbit in October to mark the 40th anniversary of the space age.

Junior High School students from the French Indian Ocean island of La Reunion and the Russian city of Naltchik signed a deal on Thursday by video link-up to build a one-third scale model of the world's first artificial satellite.

The mock-up will be flown up to Russia's MIR space station and placed in orbit by a cosmonaut on October 4, the 40th anniversary of the original launch that gave Moscow a first victory in a space race with Washington at the height of the Cold War.

The original Soviet-built Sputnik measured 58 centimetres (two ft) across with long metal prongs and carried a radio transmitter that bleeped from space, allowing scientists to track it around the globe.
The French students will build the radio transmitter that will mimic the signal of the original. The Russians will make the model of the satellite.

The first Sputnik was followed a month later by Sputnik 2, which carried the first living creature into space, the dog Laika. The breakthroughs helped the Soviet Union launch Yuri Gagarin, the first human in space in 1961.
The schools were put in touch by a French space researcher from La Reunion.
